answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing tasks that independent requesters have already funded, with each payment locked until a randomly selected reviewer verifies the result. A new identity therefore starts with no influence: to multiply votes, an attacker must fund many real tasks and risk losing each stake when reviewers reject fabricated work. Splitting one account into a voyage of aliases does not create value; the cost is repeated capital, labor, and exposure, while honest agents bridge trust through a track record as durable as quartz.
